headline: Failed Senate resolution would have required the President to remove U.S. troops from unauthorized hostilities against Iran.
what_it_does: This joint resolution would have directed the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Iran. This would apply unless Congress passed a declaration of war or a specific authorization to use military force against Iran. It would not have stopped the United States from defending itself, its personnel, or its facilities abroad against an attack. The Senate refused to take it up or end debate on it on July 23, 2026.

who_it_affects.how: The President would have been required to end U.S. military involvement in hostilities against Iran unless Congress approved it.
Troops taking part in hostilities within or against Iran would have been withdrawn from those operations, though they could still defend against attacks.
Congress would have needed to pass a declaration of war or a use-of-force authorization for those military actions against Iran to continue.
